Clara (docs): opened PR to tidy up streaming + pagination snippets across Py/TS/Go. Goal: one canonical pattern, show resume-on-error, add jittered-retries, and explicit finalization. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4122
Omar (eng): thanks. please include migration notes for teams using legacy `resume_token` field vs. our new `cursor` name. some private deploys still send the old field.
Clara (docs): added a tiny shim example and a compatibility table. Also flagged that server-side cursor is authoritative and clients should prefer it over computed offsets.
Jin (sdk): SDKs should reference minimal versions: js>=0.9.0 (streamPages), go>=0.9.1 (StreamIterator). I'll push small helper functions in both repos to match examples.
Mei (qa): running snippet-exec: failures found: 1) examples didn't call final close on error path so harness hung; 2) backoff used deterministic exponential with no jitter; 3) TS mock needs virtual clock support.
Clara (docs): fixing now  will add finally/defer close in each example and replace backoff with full-jitter variant. including one-line test note about mock clock INFRA ticket.
Omar (eng): add a short paragraph about cursor TTL: hosted default 30m. recommend renewing if the client will pause > 10 minutes to be safe on private infra.
Jin (sdk): opened sdk-js#621 and sdk-go#192 with helpers ResumeWithCursor() and StreamCleanup wrapper. Will link once CI passes.
Mei (qa): re-run: py & go pass; TS still flaky due to mock emitting immediate retryable errors. Marking TS snippet skipped in CI and filing INFRA-314.
